text:
maria.g: heads-up — noticed a regression in KV residency fairness on prod-rt-3 over the last 4h. tenant 'search-prod' is holding ~62% of resident pages during longctx runs and causing eviction storms for small-tenants. p99 tail latency for small tenants spiked ~3x. :worried:

ashok: @maria.g what changed around 02:00? any recent kernel-selection or batching tweaks deployed? :eyes:

maria.g: no new kernel changes, but we flipped the batching heuristic to prefer larger continuous batches (rollout at 01:50) to boost throughput. suspect interaction w/ longctx prefix reuse + our current per-tenant quota smoothing window.

infra-bot: Deploy 01:49 by dev/throughput-rollout detected. Canary = 10% -> 100% at 01:52. Logs: `batching.v2.enabled=true`

jun: do we have a quick pprof/heap snapshot from the affected node? want to see per-tenant heap by residency.

maria.g: uploaded quick dump to the runbook: https://internal/runbooks/kv-residency/2440009876/dump-01. Also pasted a small sample below (resident pages):

```
tenant   resident_pages   longctx_pct
search-prod   18240   0.74
ingest-batch  4200    0.15
session-lite  1200    0.05
test-guest     320    0.03
```

devon: that 74% longctx residency is the smoking gun. When batching favors larger continuous work we are keeping more KV slots hot for longer prefixes, and our quota decay window (60s) doesn't reclaim quickly enough. Two levers: reduce continuous-batch preference for multi-tenant nodes, or shorten quota smoothing / add a reactive backpressure on residency growth.

ashok: can we simulate locally? which flags to flip?

maria.g: flip `batching.v2.prefer_continuous=false` or set `kv.quota.smoothing.window_ms=15000` for tests. Repro steps in runbook.

jun: quick thought — what about proportional-share admission instead of absolute per-tenant pages? i.e. each tenant gets a share token and we evict from those that exceed share * current_total_pages. That would adapt when global working set grows. Might be cheap to prototype in the eviction sampler.

devon: +1 to prototype. For immediate mitigation, propose a short-term soft-cap: if tenant residency ratio > 0.5 and longctx_pct > 0.5 then preferentially demote oldest pages for that tenant to LRUTier2. Could add a heuristic in the pagewalk path.

maria.g: sounds good. i'll try patching a soft-cap flag on one canary host to validate impact. any concerns about correctness for long-lived model queries?

ashok: risk is harming throughput for that tenant's longctx-heavy requests (could increase its latency). but acceptable as emergency mitigation for multi-tenant fairness. we should monitor p50/p95 for that tenant after change.

infra-bot: Alert muted for node prod-rt-3. Auto-snapshot saved: s3://perf-dumps/prod-rt-3/2440009876/snap-1.tar.gz

jun: also instrument a simple metric: `kv.residency_ratio_by_tenant` (sampled every 5s) and `kv.eviction_source` (LRU vs longctx-demote) so we can correlate with tail latency.

devon: prototype demote snippet (pseudo):
```
if (tenant_residency / total_resident_pages > soft_cap_ratio && tenant_longctx_pct > 0.5) {
  demote_oldest_pages(tenant, demote_count = 256);
}
```

maria.g: rolling that to canary now with `soft_cap_ratio=0.5` and `demote_count=128`. will report back in ~5m.

ashok: thanks — if you see p99 small-tenant drop back down, we'll probably revert batching preference change for multi-tenant hosts and open a follow-up to evaluate proportional-share allocator.

maria.g: can confirm after 4m: small-tenant p99 dropped from 320ms -> 110ms on canary, search-prod p50 increased ~12%. pushing metrics and pprof. :thumbsup:

jun: good trade for now. let's assemble a short postmortem and a design doc for proportional-share quota with simulations (windowed fairness + backpressure) before we re-enable batching.v2.prefer_continuous globally.

devon: i can take the simulation. will sketch a simple O(1) sampler that keeps per-tenant counters and a decay window.

maria.g: thanks all. I'll file a ticket: INF-4521 (kv-residency: proportional-share design + short-term soft-cap rollout notes).

infra-bot: Ticket INF-4521 created by maria.g: https://issues/internal/INF-4521

ashok: nice work. follow up items: (1) simulation (devon) (2) metric rollout (jun) (3) revert batching preference on multi-tenant hosts or keep flag gated by node_label (maria).
